data.exact_reserve_text: The older years have seen reserve volatility during CY16 which has been explained in comments set out in the year of account review below; as to be expected there are no premium movements of any note on the run-off years 2012 and 2013 to offset these reserve deteriorations and the earning out of premiums in 2014 YOA has also been lower than the recalibration of ultimate reserve losses. Movement in the year comprises claims charges of GBP (2.5)m, additional reinsurance accruals of GBP (0.3)m, GBP (0.2)m of expense and provision charges and investment income of GBP 0.1m. During the year ended 31 December 2016 unfavourable actual versus expected experience was noted in the review carried out for the six months ended 30 June 2016, which led to the to the development pattern and prior loss assumptions being revised and additional IBNR being booked. For this year of account additional claims reserves, gross and net, have also been set aside for a large liability claim, arising from a serious sporting accident. Movement in 2016 comprises claims charges of GBP (5.0)m, GBP (0.4)m of additional reinsurance accruals, GBP 1.5m of expense and provision credits less charges, investment income of GBP 0.4m and GBP (1.3)m of exchange movements. During the year ended 31 December 2016 unfavourable actual versus expected experience was noted in the review carried out for the six months ended 30 June 2016, which led to the to the development pattern and prior loss assumptions being revised and additional IBNR being booked. A large Australian liability claim was settled in the year ended 31 December 2016, and two more events of significance remain under scrutiny.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant strengthening of prior year reserves in 2016, primarily driven by adverse development across the 2011-2014 underwriting years. This included reserve volatility, deteriorations, and recalibration of ultimate reserve losses for older years. Specific factors contributing to this strengthening were unfavourable actual versus expected experience, revisions to development patterns and prior loss assumptions, and additional IBNR bookings for the 2012 and 2013 years of account. Notable events included a late Contingency claim from 2015, a large liability claim from a serious sporting accident in 2013, and a large Australian liability claim from 2012, along with two other significant events from 2012 under scrutiny. The liability book, in particular, showed continued uncertainty over its ultimate loss ratio and outstanding reserving exposure.
